productionAssessment.scope: Read-only pg_proc function definition and execution privileges; no function invocation or account data reads
productionAssessment.finding: Deployed body clears must_change_password based solely on auth.uid(); same confirmed vulnerable implementation

chartInvestigation.scope: Instrumented unchanged production build with real isolated Auth sessions
chartInvestigation.serverChart: Money in, money out and the net for 12 months
chartInvestigation.finding: Intermittent Next client search-parameter transition stalls after the correct server response; also reproduced a 65-second timeout, and observed an aborted RSC request in another attempt. Both successful and stalled transitions occurred with standard 3600-second tokens. Neither changing token duration nor waiting for document load fixes it.
chartInvestigation.correction: Only range links use native document navigation, anchored at the chart. A chart-control mount effect restores that anchor after streamed content arrives. Existing searchParams parsing, SVG rendering, RPC and calculations are unchanged. The twelve-month axis keeps six spaced labels, with all twelve data buckets and tooltips retained; the six-month view is unchanged.
chartInvestigation.limit: No claim about the precise internal Next.js scheduler cause; the failure is localized to client navigation rather than chart data or search parameter parsing.

notificationInvestigation.scope: Instrumented real isolated Auth sessions against unchanged and candidate production builds; all writes synthetic
notificationInvestigation.baselineComponent: MarkAllRead: useTransition pending drives the button; await markNotificationsRead(); router.refresh() inside the same transition

baselineReproduction.everyFailure: ownRead=true, peerUnread=true; aria-busy stayed true past 45 seconds
baselineReproduction.finding: The action POST returned HTTP 200 within 110-155ms and the client reached router.refresh() 2-6ms later, so the action promise always resolved. The transition stayed pending because the router update it was bound to never committed.

earlierCandidateResult.detail: Removing the explicit client refresh did not resolve the intermittent member timeout. The speculative component change was reverted.

isolation.change: Component-owned busy state; router.refresh() outside the transition
isolation.note: aria-busy was released after about 290ms in every attempt, so the control no longer hangs; the staff page content still did not update.

isolation.change: Component-owned busy state; server revalidation only, no client refresh

isolation.note: Revalidation path coverage is not the cause.

isolation.change: Removed both revalidatePath calls; router.refresh() only

isolation.note: The Suspense boundary is not the cause.

isolation.note: Removes the server action, transitions and revalidation from the question entirely.

isolation.note: The client router and the staff route tree are healthy.

Same page without the notification list

isolation.note: Isolates the defect to the size of the rendered list rather than Icon, Link or relative times.

listLengthSweep.finding: Correlated with payload size, with no clean threshold; the failure is intermittent rather than deterministic.

serverResponse.checked: Action POST response body captured and replayed
serverResponse.finding: The server returned the corrected tree on every attempt, including attempts the client did not apply. Reloading the page always showed the saved state.

notificationInvestigation.cause: The button was disabled and busy for as long as the React transition stayed pending, and the transition was bound to a client router update that the Next 15.5.24 app router applies only intermittently on the notifications routes - most often on the staff route, whose rendered list is larger. The database write, its ownership checks and the server response were correct in every observed failure.
notificationInvestigation.correction: The control now owns its busy state and settles it on the action result, refuses a second request while one is open, reports a failure and allows a retry, and shows the saved state through a native navigation. The server action, the RPC, revalidation and permissions are unchanged.
notificationInvestigation.limit: No claim is made about the internal Next.js cause. The defect is localized to the client application of refreshed trees, and is the same client-navigation defect the dashboard chart ranges navigate around.

verification.runs: 3 independent runs on the final production build of the clean stack

passwordFormFinding.scope: Real browser submissions of the signed-in change-password form at 390x900, staff /staff/profile and member /profile
passwordFormFinding.breakdown: Two independent runs of eight attempts: 4/8 and 1/8 displayed the error
passwordFormFinding.serverBehaviour: Correct in all 16 attempts: the action POST returned HTTP 200, the auth.password_changed audit count was unchanged and the new password never became valid
passwordFormFinding.clientBehaviour: The attempts that displayed "Your current password is incorrect." were the ones where a tree update followed the POST response; in the others no error was displayed at all
passwordFormFinding.finding: The same intermittent client tree-update defect behind BKC-03 also suppresses this form’s validation errors, so a wrong current password usually produces no visible feedback. The error text and selectors are correct; the previous certification attributed these two browser failures to an icon-prefixed selector mistake, which this run does not reproduce — the broad run and the documented focused recheck both fail.
passwordFormFinding.scopeNote: Outside BKC-03 and not changed in this branch: the form is part of the BKC-01 security remediation, so a remedy needs its own review. A native navigation cannot carry a transient validation message, so the likely remedy is to verify the current password without relying on a server-action tree update.
